what: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: R package computing climate indices daily weather observations. Takes vectors temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind data returns tidy data frames - file wrangling, class coercion, API calls.

title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: Climate indices standardised summary statistics reduce daily weather observations meaningful measures climate conditions. single year weather data one station 365 rows temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity readings. Climate indices compress interpretable numbers: many frost days occurred, long growing season lasted, whether region drought. indices matter climate science connects real economy. Energy companies use heating cooling degree days forecast demand. Agricultural ministries track growing degree days frost dates. Water authorities monitor SPI SPEI drought indices. Urban planners measure heat index exceedances. Insurance actuaries count extreme precipitation events. Viticulturists use Huglin Winkler indices assess grape-growing potential. Fire services monitor fire weather indices. definitions come international standards bodies - WMO Expert Team Climate Change Detection Indices (ETCCDI) defines 27 core indices, Expert Team Sector-specific Climate Indices (ET-SCI) extends health, agriculture, energy domains, individual research communities added domain-specific measures like SPEI drought Huglin viticulture.

what: Getting started: where to get the data
title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: climatekit computes indices weather data provide. doesn’t download anything : bring data, maths. already data (CSV, database export, Excel file), need numeric vector observations date vector: don’t data yet, easiest way get started readnoaa, downloads free daily weather observations NOAA’s global archive 100,000+ stations. API key needed: long numeric vector date vector, climatekit work .
code: library(climatekit)  # Read your own data weather <- read.csv("my_weather_station.csv")  # Compute frost days ck_frost_days(weather$tmin, weather$date) install.packages("readnoaa")  # or devtools::install_github("charlescoverdale/readnoaa") library(readnoaa) library(climatekit)  # Step 1: Find a station near you noaa_nearby(lat = 51.5, lon = -0.1, radius_km = 25) #>        station                    name latitude longitude distance_km #>   UKE00105915     LONDON WEATHER CENTRE   51.517    -0.117        1.4  # Step 2: Download daily data weather <- noaa_daily("UKE00105915", "2020-01-01", "2024-12-31",                       datatypes = c("TMAX", "TMIN", "PRCP"))  # Step 3: Compute indices ck_frost_days(weather$tmin, weather$date, period = "annual") ck_spi(weather$prcp, weather$date, scale = 3) ck_heating_degree_days((weather$tmax + weather$tmin) / 2, weather$date)

title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: R methods, scattered across half dozen packages incompatible interfaces: want frost days, degree days, SPI, Huglin index analysis, currently need four packages four different input formats four different output structures. One wants S4 object, another wants matrix, third wants separate vectors, none return data frame dates attached. climatekit replaces single interface: vectors , data frames . Every function takes kind input (numeric vector + date vector), every function returns kind output (data frame period, value, index, unit columns), 35 indices span temperature, precipitation, drought, agroclimatic, comfort categories.
code: # Without climatekit: four packages, four input formats, four output structures library(climdex.pcic) ci <- climdexInput.raw(tmax = ..., tmin = ..., prec = ..., ...)  # S4 object fd <- climdex.fd(ci)  # returns named numeric vector, no dates  library(SPEI) spi_result <- spi(ts(monthly_precip, frequency = 12), 3)  # returns S4, needs ts()  library(ClimInd) gdd <- gdd(tavg_vector, 10)  # returns raw numeric, no metadata  # With climatekit: one package, one interface library(climatekit) ck_frost_days(tmin, dates)                     # → data.frame ck_spi(precip, dates, scale = 3)               # → data.frame ck_growing_degree_days(tavg, dates, base = 10)  # → data.frame ck_huglin(tmin, tmax, dates, lat = 45)          # → data.frame

title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
code: # The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) fits a gamma distribution to # monthly precipitation totals over a rolling window, then transforms to # standard normal deviates. Values below -1 indicate moderate drought, # below -1.5 severe drought, below -2 extreme drought.  dates_long <- seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), as.Date("2024-12-31"), by = "day") set.seed(42) precip <- rgamma(length(dates_long), shape = 2, rate = 0.5)  spi <- ck_spi(precip, dates_long, scale = 3) head(spi) #>       period      value index        unit #>   2015-03-01 -0.2891577   spi dimensionless #>   2015-04-01  0.4458927   spi dimensionless #>   ...  # SPEI adds evapotranspiration to capture temperature-driven drought pet <- ck_pet(tmin, tmax, lat = 51.5, dates = dates)

what: What wine regions does a climate support?
title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
code: # The Huglin heliothermal index classifies grape-growing potential: # < 1500: too cool for viticulture # 1500-1800: cool climate (Champagne, Mosel) # 1800-2100: temperate (Burgundy, Oregon) # 2100-2400: warm (Bordeaux, Napa) # > 2400: hot (Barossa, Southern Spain)  dates_gs <- seq(as.Date("2024-04-01"), as.Date("2024-09-30"), by = "day") set.seed(42) tmin_gs <- rnorm(length(dates_gs), mean = 12, sd = 3) tmax_gs <- tmin_gs + runif(length(dates_gs), 8, 15)  ck_huglin(tmin_gs, tmax_gs, dates_gs, lat = 45) #>       period    value  index        unit #>   2024-01-01 2129.284 huglin degree-days  # Winkler index (wine region classification) tavg_gs <- (tmin_gs + tmax_gs) / 2 ck_winkler(tavg_gs, dates_gs)

This is useful in loops, Shiny apps, # or any workflow where the index is selected at runtime.  weather <- data.frame(   dates = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:364,   tmin = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 365)) * 15 + 2,   tmax = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 365)) * 15 + 12,   precip = rgamma(365, shape = 0.5, rate = 0.2) )  # Compute any index by name ck_compute(weather, "frost_days") ck_compute(weather, "total_precip", period = "monthly")  # See all available indices ck_available() #>                 index      category          unit #>            frost_days   temperature          days #>              ice_days   temperature          days #>          summer_days    temperature          days #>    tropical_nights     temperature          days #>    ...

title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: Every function follows pattern: Input: Numeric vectors + date vector. special objects, S4 classes, preprocessing required. Output: tidy data frame consistent columns. outputs join cleanly period date columns, can compute multiple indices merge single analysis data frame.
code: ck_frost_days(   tmin = c(-2, 3, -1, 5, -3),   dates = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:4 ) # Period-aggregated indices return: #>   period (Date) | value (numeric) | index (character) | unit (character)  # Daily indices (PET, wind chill, heat index) return: #>   date (Date) | value (numeric) | index (character) | unit (character)

title: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought
text: ck_ prefix - short, distinctive, won’t collide packages. Easy type easy autocomplete. Vectors , data frames - simplest possible interface. custom S4 objects construct, ts() coercion, zoo xts dependencies. column temperatures column dates, can use package. API calls - pure computation package. download data. Pair readnoaa data source. separation keeps package fast, testable, CRAN-friendly. heavy dependencies - depends cli, stats, tools. tidyverse, Rcpp, external system libraries. Period aggregation - indices naturally period-aggregated (e.g. “many frost days year?”). aggregated functions accept period = "annual" (default) period = "monthly". NA handling - functions handle missing values gracefully. NAs excluded counts aggregations, matching behaviour researchers expect.

what: climatekit: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought — climatekit-package
title: climatekit: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought — climatekit-package
text: Compute 35+ standard climate indices daily weather observations. Includes temperature indices (frost days, ice days, growing degree days), precipitation indices (dry spells, heavy precipitation, intensity), drought indices (Standardized Precipitation Index, Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index), agroclimatic indices (Huglin, Winkler, Branas), comfort indices (wind chill, heat index, humidex, fire danger). functions accept vectors observations dates return tidy data frames metadata. Implements 'ET-SCI' Expert Team Sector-specific Climate Indices definitions applicable. external API calls; pairs data packages 'readnoaa' acquisition.

title: climatekit: Unified Climate Indices for Temperature, Precipitation, and Drought — climatekit-package

title: climatekit 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-03-23 Initial release. 10 temperature indices: frost days, ice days, summer days, tropical nights, growing season length, heating/cooling/growing degree days, diurnal temperature range, warm spell duration. 8 precipitation indices: consecutive dry/wet days, total precipitation, heavy/heavy precipitation days, max 1-day 5-day precipitation, precipitation intensity (SDII). 3 drought indices: Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), potential evapotranspiration (Hargreaves method). 5 agroclimatic indices: Huglin, Winkler, Branas, first/last frost dates. 4 comfort indices: wind chill, heat index, humidex, fire danger index. Generic dispatcher ck_compute() programmatic index selection. ck_available() ck_metadata() index discovery. ck_convert_temp() temperature unit conversion.
